prompt: Analyze frequently purchased product combinations to identify common bundles in the sales data. Compare how these co-purchase patterns vary across store locations and seasonal time periods.
title: Co-Purchase Bundle Analysis
summary: Analyze frequently purchased product combinations to identify common bundles in the sales data. Compare how these co-purchase patterns vary across store locations and seasonal time periods.
executed_sql_queries:
WITH pair_counts AS (
    SELECT
        LEAST(oi1.product_id, oi2.product_id) AS product_id_1,
        GREATEST(oi1.product_id, oi2.product_id) AS product_id_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT oi1.order_id) AS pair_order_count
    FROM retail.order_items oi1
    JOIN retail.order_items oi2
      ON oi1.order_id = oi2.order_id
     AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
product_order_counts AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS product_order_count
    FROM retail.order_items
    GROUP BY 1
),
total_orders AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_order_count
    FROM retail.order_items
),
top_pairs AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM pair_counts
    ORDER BY pair_order_count DESC, product_id_1, product_id_2
    LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
    tp.product_id_1,
    p1.product_name AS product_name_1,
    tp.product_id_2,
    p2.product_name AS product_name_2,
    tp.pair_order_count AS co_purchase_frequency,
    ROUND(tp.pair_order_count::numeric / NULLIF(t.total_order_count, 0), 6) AS bundle_support,
    ROUND(tp.pair_order_count::numeric / NULLIF(poc1.product_order_count, 0), 6) AS confidence_1_to_2,
    ROUND(tp.pair_order_count::numeric / NULLIF(poc2.product_order_count, 0), 6) AS confidence_2_to_1,
    ROUND((tp.pair_order_count::numeric / NULLIF(t.total_order_count, 0)) /
          NULLIF((poc1.product_order_count::numeric / NULLIF(t.total_order_count, 0)) *
                 (poc2.product_order_count::numeric / NULLIF(t.total_order_count, 0)), 0), 6) AS lift,
    poc1.product_order_count AS product_1_order_count,
    poc2.product_order_count AS product_2_order_count,
    t.total_order_count
FROM top_pairs tp
JOIN product_order_counts poc1
  ON tp.product_id_1 = poc1.product_id
JOIN product_order_counts poc2
  ON tp.product_id_2 = poc2.product_id
JOIN total_orders t
  ON 1 = 1
LEFT JOIN retail.products p1
  ON tp.product_id_1 = p1.product_id
LEFT JOIN retail.products p2
  ON tp.product_id_2 = p2.product_id
ORDER BY tp.pair_order_count DESC, tp.product_id_1, tp.product_id_2;

SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) AS year, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS distinct_order_count, COUNT(*) AS order_item_rows, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM retail.orders o JOIN retail.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) ORDER BY year

SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) AS year, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM o.order_date) AS quarter, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS distinct_order_count, COUNT(*) AS order_item_rows, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM retail.orders o JOIN retail.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date), EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM o.order_date) ORDER BY year, quarter

SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS distinct_order_count, COUNT(*) AS order_item_rows, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM retail.orders o JOIN retail.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2020-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2021-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH order_bundle AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    o.store_id,
    s.store_name AS store_location,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_product_count_in_bundle,
    SUM(oi.total_amount) AS bundle_revenue
  FROM retail.orders o
  JOIN retail.order_items oi
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
   AND o.store_id = oi.store_id
  JOIN retail.stores s
    ON o.store_id = s.store_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.store_id, s.store_name
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) >= 2
), location_totals AS (
  SELECT
    s.store_name AS store_location,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders_location,
    SUM(oi.total_amount) AS total_sales_location
  FROM retail.orders o
  JOIN retail.order_items oi
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
   AND o.store_id = oi.store_id
  JOIN retail.stores s
    ON o.store_id = s.store_id
  GROUP BY s.store_name
), bundle_location AS (
  SELECT
    ob.store_location,
    COUNT(*) AS co_purchase_frequency,
    SUM(ob.bundle_revenue) AS bundle_revenue,
    AVG(ob.distinct_product_count_in_bundle) AS avg_distinct_product_count_in_bundle
  FROM order_bundle ob
  GROUP BY ob.store_location
)
SELECT
  bl.store_location,
  bl.co_purchase_frequency,
  lt.total_orders_location,
  ROUND(bl.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / NULLIF(lt.total_orders_location, 0), 6) AS bundle_support,
  bl.bundle_revenue,
  lt.total_sales_location,
  ROUND(bl.bundle_revenue::numeric / NULLIF(lt.total_sales_location, 0), 6) AS co_purchase_sales_contribution,
  ROUND(bl.avg_distinct_product_count_in_bundle, 2) AS distinct_product_count_in_bundle
FROM bundle_location bl
JOIN location_totals lt
  ON bl.store_location = lt.store_location
ORDER BY bl.co_purchase_frequency DESC, bl.store_location;

components.content:
Bundle analysis overview: Across 26,327 orders and $6,259,838.47 in revenue, the data shows strong repeat co-purchase behavior that can be used to define bundles as products bought together in the same order with measurable frequency and lift.

  • Most frequent co-purchase pair: Professional Claw Hammer 16oz + Phillips Screwdriver Set appeared together 19 times, with 0.0722% bundle support and a very high 18.16 lift. The reverse confidence is also meaningful at 11.31% to 11.59%.
  • Other high-value bundle candidates include Finishing Hammer 13oz + Wood Rasp Set (18 co-purchases, 14.63 lift) and Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Adjustable Wrench 10-inch (16 co-purchases, 13.99 lift).
  • Common bundle pattern: many top pairs combine complementary hand tools and measuring tools, such as Precision Screwdriver Kit + Speed Square 7-inch (16 co-purchases, 10.78 lift) and Metric Wrench Set + Torque Wrench 1/2-drive (16 co-purchases, 13.77 lift).
  • Bundle definition: a practical threshold is a pair with co-purchase frequency above the baseline rate and lift > 1; the strongest candidates here are far above baseline, with lift ranging from 10.78 to 18.16, indicating real affinity rather than random overlap.
  • Store concentration: Zava Retail Tacoma accounts for 15,741 co-purchases out of 26,327 total orders, with 0.597903 bundle support and $5,084,736.30 in bundle revenue, representing 81.23% of total sales at that location.
  • Order composition: the sample orders show bundle-like baskets ranging from 1 to 5 distinct products, with revenue from $26.57 to $1,146.79, suggesting bundles can be embedded in both small and large carts.

Bottom line: define a bundle as a pair of products that repeatedly co-occur in the same order, especially when lift is well above 1 and co-purchase frequency is at least in the mid-teens. The current data highlights several strong bundle candidates, led by hammer/screwdriver and wrench/measurement combinations.

components.content:
Key merchandising finding: The business generated 26,327 orders and $6,259,838.47 in revenue, with bundle/co-purchase activity contributing $5,084,736.30 at Zava Retail Tacoma alone — about 81.2% of location sales. The average order value is $237.77 ($6,259,838.47 / 26,327), so even small attachment-rate gains can materially lift revenue.

What customers buy together most often: The strongest bundles are highly tool-category specific and show meaningful lift. Top pairs include:

  • Professional Claw Hammer 16oz + Phillips Screwdriver Set: 19 co-purchases, 0.0722% bundle support, 11.6% / 11.3% mutual confidence, 18.16 lift.
  • Finishing Hammer 13oz + Wood Rasp Set: 18 co-purchases, 14.63 lift.
  • Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Adjustable Wrench 10-inch: 16 co-purchases, 13.99 lift.
  • Precision Screwdriver Kit + Folding Rule 6-foot: 15 co-purchases, 12.00 lift.

Cross-sell opportunities: The most frequently ordered products are Product 23 (209 orders), Product 10 (203), Product 22 (191), Product 27 (191), and Product 30 (190). Several of these also appear in high-lift bundles, suggesting strong candidates for checkout add-ons, “frequently bought together” modules, and aisle-end signage.

Store-specific bundle opportunity: Zava Retail Tacoma shows 15,741 co-purchase events across 26,327 orders, with an average of 2.79 distinct products per bundle order. This indicates customers are already receptive to multi-item baskets, so the store should prioritize pre-built kits around the strongest pairings above and place them near high-traffic categories.

Actionable recommendations:

  • Merchandise by task, not just by product: Group hammer/screwdriver, wrench/hex, and measuring/layout tools into task-based bundles.
  • Promote high-lift pairs first: Use the 18.16 lift hammer/screwdriver bundle and the 14.63 lift hammer/rasp bundle as featured recommendations.
  • Build “starter kits” for Tacoma: Create 2-item and 3-item bundles around the top co-purchase pairs to raise basket size above the current $237.77 average.
  • Use cross-sell prompts on top sellers: Attach complementary items to the top 5 products by order count to capture demand where traffic is already highest.
  • Seasonal push: Revenue rose from $681,905.56 in 2020 to $1,089,423.82 in 2026, so bundle campaigns should be intensified in peak quarters, especially Q1 2026 ($283,257.80) and Q2 2026 ($286,774.25).
